questions.text: What is the typical forward barrier potential of a Silicon (Si) PN junction diode at $25^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.explanation: Silicon PN diodes have a nominal forward barrier potential of approximately $0.7\,\text{V}$. Germanium (Ge) diodes exhibit approximately $0.3\,\text{V}$.

questions.text: A silicon diode is connected in series with a $1\,\text{k}\Omega$ resistor and a $10\,\text{V}$ DC voltage source. Assuming a forward voltage drop of $0.7\,\text{V}$, calculate the circuit current $I$.
questions.explanation: By Kirchhoff's Voltage Law: $$V_S - V_D - I R = 0$$ $$10\,\text{V} - 0.7\,\text{V} = I(1000\,\Omega)$$ $$I = \frac{9.3\,\text{V}}{1000\,\Omega} = 9.3\,\text{mA}$$

questions.text: Which semiconductor majority carrier type is responsible for electric current conduction in an N-type semiconductor material?
questions.explanation: N-type semiconductor is doped with pentavalent donor impurities (such as Phosphorus, Arsenic, or Antimony), which provide an excess of free conduction band electrons as majority carriers.

questions.text: A full-wave center-tapped rectifier circuit has a transformer secondary voltage of $24\,\text{V}_{\text{rms}}$ from the center tap to either end. Neglecting diode drop, what is the Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) rating required for each diode?
questions.explanation: For a center-tapped full-wave rectifier: $$V_m = 24 \times \sqrt{2} \approx 33.94\,\text{V}$$ The Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) across the non-conducting diode is: $$\text{PIV} = 2 V_m = 2(33.94\,\text{V}) \approx 67.9\,\text{V}$$

questions.text: In a Zener diode operating in its breakdown region, what happens to the voltage across the diode as the reverse current increases?
questions.explanation: In the avalanche/Zener breakdown region, a Zener diode maintains an essentially constant voltage $V_Z$ across its terminals over a wide variation of reverse breakdown current, making it ideal for voltage regulation.
